## Atoms

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.html

Small additions to the base layer, for what a native element cannot express on its own. A level of [Atomic Design](https://atomicdesign.bradfrost.com/); APIs follow the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api).

### Our choices

From [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md).

- **Our choice:** one `data-<atom>` attribute per atom, whose value is a space-separated list matched with [`~=`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Attribute_selectors). One attribute is one API to learn, it reads as a sentence (`data-button="primary small"`), and it cannot pile up like modifier classes.
- **Our choice:** `data-button` with no variant word keeps the native default (a submit button is primary, everything else is secondary), so M1 markup keeps working and the attribute is only needed when the native type does not match the emphasis you want.
- **Our choice:** the quiet button uses the accent color for its text, so it still reads as interactive without a border. Use it next to other buttons, not inside running text, where a real link belongs.
- **Our choice:** primary buttons add an inner focus ring in their text color on top of the shared outline, so the indicator contrasts with the fill as well as the surface. This is the double-ring technique described in [WCAG technique C40](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C40).
- **Our choice:** small buttons are 32px tall: below the 44px default, above the [24px minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html).
- **Our choice:** `aria-disabled="true"` looks exactly like `disabled`. Prefer native `disabled`; use `aria-disabled` when users should be able to reach the control and read why it is unavailable.
- **Our choice:** the field's error text starts with the word "Error:" in the markup, rather than a CSS icon, so every user and every screen reader gets it with no extra API. Invalid controls also get a thick start border, a shape change as well as a color change.
- **Our choice:** errors are tied to controls with `aria-describedby`, not `aria-errormessage`, because `aria-describedby` has broader screen reader support today (see the support notes on [MDN `aria-errormessage`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-errormessage)).
- **Our choice:** the switch is the native checkbox with `role="switch"`, drawn with `appearance: none` and one pseudo-element. The thumb moves and changes color, and forced-colors mode gets explicit system colors.
- **Our choice:** badge tones are 8% of the tone mixed into the surface, with the tone as text. The tinted surfaces are derived tokens (`--dui-color-*-surface`), so a theme that changes the surface or a tone re-tints badges with no extra overrides.
- **Our choice:** a field is an atom here, not a molecule, because a control is not usable without its label, hint and error. Larger compositions (forms, cards, headers) are molecules and organisms for later milestones.

### Not shipped, and why

| Candidate | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Divider | Cut. `<hr>` is the native thematic break and is already styled in the base layer. A class would duplicate it. |
| Avatar | Cut. There is no standard or APG pattern for it; it is an `<img alt>` with a radius and a size, which the base layer and one line of your CSS already give. Revisit with a real use case (initials fallback, image loading). |
| Icon sizing | Cut. domestic-ui ships no icon set, so there is nothing to size consistently yet. Inside buttons, icons already line up through the button's `inline-flex` and `gap`. |
| Danger button variant | Not added. Not requested, and a destructive action is better marked by its label and a confirmation `<dialog>` than by color. Easy to add later as one more variant word. |
| Spinner for loading | Not added. The honest state is the changed label plus `aria-busy`; a spinner that replaces the label hides it from everyone. |

## Text helpers

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/text.html

Lead, small and muted text helpers from domestic-ui, with copyable markup.

### Live example

#### Lead paragraph

```html
<p data-text="lead">Plan your week in five minutes. Everything else stays out of the way.</p>
<p>Regular body text follows at the normal size.</p>
```

#### Small and muted

```html
<p data-text="small">Prices include tax.</p>
<p data-text="muted">Shared with 3 people.</p>
<p data-text="small muted">Last updated <time datetime="2026-05-03">3 May 2026</time>.</p>
```

### Attributes

`data-text="lead | small | muted"` (combinable)

```text
data-text="lead | small | muted"
Values are a space-separated list, so they combine: data-text="small muted".
```

- Values combine: `data-text="small muted"`.
- Size and color only. For meaning, use [`<small>`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-small-element), `<strong>` or `<em>`.

### Accessibility

- Muted text uses `--dui-color-text-muted`, tested at 4.5:1 on every surface ([WCAG 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)).

### Specifications

- [WHATWG text-level semantics](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html)
- [WCAG 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)
- [WHATWG the small element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-small-element)

### See also

- [Atoms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/components/atoms/text.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/text.css), [`examples/atoms/text.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/text.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Typography](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography)
- [Material Design 3: Typography](https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Typography](https://vercel.com/geist/typography)

## Quiet link

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/link.html

A link that takes the surrounding text color and keeps its underline, for dense UI.

### Live example

#### In a table

```html
<section data-scroll="inline" aria-labelledby="orders-caption" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="orders-caption">Recent orders</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr><th scope="col">Order</th><th scope="col">Customer</th><th scope="col">Total</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td><a href="#table-title" data-link="quiet">#1042</a></td><td>Ada Lovelace</td><td>€120.00</td></tr>
      <tr><td><a href="#table-title" data-link="quiet">#1041</a></td><td>Alan Turing</td><td>€48.50</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</section>
```

#### In muted metadata

```html
<p data-text="small muted">Posted by <a href="#meta-title" data-link="quiet">Grace Hopper</a> in <a href="#meta-title" data-link="quiet">Compilers</a>.</p>
```

### Attributes

`data-link="quiet"` on `<a href>`

```text
data-link="quiet"   on <a href>
```

- For dense UI, such as table cells, footers and metadata, where many accent-colored links would be noisy.
- Visited links keep the surrounding color too.

### Accessibility

- The underline stays, so color is never the only cue ([WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)).
- The link takes the surrounding text color, which already has 4.5:1 contrast.

### Specifications

- [WHATWG `a`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element)
- [WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)

### See also

- [Atoms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/components/atoms/link.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/link.css), [`examples/atoms/link.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/link.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Buttons

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/button.html

Button variants and sizes, links styled as buttons, and disabled and loading states.

### Live example

#### Variants

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-button="primary">Primary</button>
  <button type="button" data-button="secondary">Secondary</button>
  <button type="button" data-button="quiet">Quiet</button>
</div>
```

#### Native default

```html
<form action="#native-title" class="cluster">
  <button type="submit">Publish</button>
  <button type="submit" name="draft" value="1" data-button="secondary">Save draft</button>
  <button type="reset" data-button="quiet">Clear</button>
</form>
```

#### Sizes

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-button="primary small">Small</button>
  <button type="button" data-button="primary">Default</button>
  <button type="button" data-button="primary large">Large</button>
</div>
```

#### Links that look like buttons

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <a href="#links-title" data-button="primary">Create account</a>
  <a href="#links-title" data-button="secondary">Read the guide</a>
  <a href="#links-title" data-button="quiet">Skip for now</a>
</div>
```

#### Disabled

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-button="primary" disabled>Delete</button>
  <button type="button" disabled>Archive</button>
</div>
```

#### Disabled but focusable

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-button="primary" aria-disabled="true" aria-describedby="publish-why">Publish</button>
  <p id="publish-why" data-text="small muted">Add a title before publishing.</p>
</div>
```

#### Loading

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" id="save-demo" data-button="primary">Save changes</button>
  <p id="save-status" role="status" data-text="small muted"></p>
</div>
```

### Attributes

`data-button="[primary | secondary | quiet] [small | large]"` on `<button>`, `<input type=submit|button|reset>`, `<a href>`; states `disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"`, `aria-busy="true"`

```text
data-button="[primary | secondary | quiet] [small | large]"
A space-separated list: at most one variant word and one size word.
Works on <button>, <input type="submit|button|reset"> and <a href>.
No variant word keeps the native default: type="submit" is primary,
other buttons and links are secondary.
```

- On `<a href>`, it looks like a button and keeps link semantics.

### States

```text
disabled              Native. Removed from the tab order, not submitted.
aria-disabled="true"  Looks disabled and is exposed as disabled, but stays
                      focusable so a description can explain why. Your script
                      must ignore activation. https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#focusabilityofdisabledcontrols
                      https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-disabled
aria-busy="true"      Work in progress. Change the visible label too
                      ("Saving…") and announce the result in a role="status"
                      region; nothing here hides the label.
                      https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-busy
```

### Sizes

```text
default and large are at least 44px tall. small is 32px: below the
44px default but above the 24px minimum of WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum).
https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html
```

### Focus

```text
every variant keeps the base :focus-visible outline. Filled (primary)
buttons add an inner ring in their text color, so the indicator contrasts
with the fill as well as with the surface (WCAG 1.4.11, 2.4.13).
https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html
```

### Motion

```text
background and border colors fade over --dui-motion-duration-
fast with --dui-motion-easing-standard. Focus rings, disabled and
aria-busy change at once: they are essential feedback.
```

### Accessibility

- `aria-disabled="true"` stays focusable, so a description can say why; your script must ignore activation ([APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#focusabilityofdisabledcontrols)).
- With `aria-busy="true"`, also change the label ("Saving…") and announce the result in a `role="status"` region.

### Specifications

- [WHATWG `button`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-button-element)
- [APG Button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/)
- [APG focusability of disabled controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#focusabilityofdisabledcontrols)
- [MDN `aria-disabled`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-disabled)
- [MDN `aria-busy`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-busy)
- [WCAG 2.5.8](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)
- [WCAG Focus appearance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html)

### See also

- [Atoms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/components/atoms/button.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/button.css), [`examples/atoms/button.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/button.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons)
- [Material Design 3: Buttons](https://m3.material.io/components/buttons/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Button](https://vercel.com/geist/button)

## Switch

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/switch.html

An on/off switch built on a native checkbox with role switch, following the APG Switch pattern.

### Live example

#### Off, on and disabled

```html
<div class="stack" style="--stack-gap: 0">
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="alerts"> Email alerts</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="digest" checked> Weekly digest</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="beta" disabled> Beta features</label>
</div>
```

#### In a fieldset

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Privacy</legend>
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="profile-public" checked> Public profile</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="show-email"> Show email address</label>
</fieldset>
```

### Attributes

`role="switch"` on `<input type="checkbox">`

```text
role="switch"   on <input type="checkbox">; no class needed.
```

- Keep the label the same in both states; the state is on or off.
- Wrap the input in its `<label>` so the whole label is the click target.

### Motion

```text
the track color fades over --dui-motion-duration-fast; the
thumb slides for that duration times --dui-motion-movement, so with
reduced motion it jumps and the color change stays. The state itself
never waits on the transition.
```

### Accessibility

- The native checkbox brings focus, <kbd>Space</kbd> to toggle, form submission and `:checked`. `role="switch"` makes assistive technology announce on and off ([APG Switch](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/), [ARIA in HTML](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-input-checkbox)).
- State is not color alone: the thumb moves and changes color, and the track fills ([WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)).
- Track border and thumb have 3:1 contrast with the surface ([WCAG 1.4.11](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)).
- In [forced colors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors), system colors keep both states visible.

### Specifications

- [APG Switch](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/)
- [ARIA in HTML](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-input-checkbox)
- [MDN `switch` role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/switch_role)
- [MDN `forced-colors`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors)
- [WCAG Use of color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)
- [WCAG Non text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)

### See also

- [Atoms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/components/atoms/switch.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/switch.css), [`examples/atoms/switch.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/switch.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Toggles](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toggles)
- [Material Design 3: Switch](https://m3.material.io/components/switch/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Switch](https://vercel.com/geist/switch)

## Field

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/field.html

Label, control, hint and error message wired with aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

### Live example

#### With a hint

```html
<div data-field>
  <label for="f-name">Display name</label>
  <input id="f-name" name="display-name" type="text" autocomplete="nickname" aria-describedby="f-name-hint">
  <p id="f-name-hint" data-field="hint">Shown next to your comments.</p>
</div>
```

#### With a hint and an error

```html
<div data-field>
  <label for="f-email">Email</label>
  <input id="f-email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" value="ada@" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="f-email-hint f-email-error">
  <p id="f-email-hint" data-field="hint">We only use this to reply.</p>
  <p id="f-email-error" data-field="error">Error: enter an email address like name@example.com.</p>
</div>
```

#### Native validation

```html
<form action="#native-title" class="stack">
  <div data-field>
    <label for="f-code">Invite code</label>
    <input id="f-code" name="code" type="text" required minlength="6" aria-describedby="f-code-hint">
    <p id="f-code-hint" data-field="hint">Six characters or more.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="cluster">
    <button type="submit">Join</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

#### A group with an error

```html
<fieldset data-field aria-describedby="f-size-error">
  <legend>Size</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="s"> Small</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="m"> Medium</label>
  <p id="f-size-error" data-field="error">Error: choose a size.</p>
</fieldset>
```

### Attributes

`data-field` on the wrapper, `data-field="hint"` and `data-field="error"` on the messages

```text
data-field              on the wrapper (a <div>, or a <fieldset> for groups)
data-field="hint"       on the hint
data-field="error"      on the error message
```

- The wrapper is a `<div>`, or a `<fieldset>` for a group of controls.
- Hide an error that does not apply with `hidden`, and remove its id from `aria-describedby`.

### Accessibility

- `<label for>` names the control ([WCAG 1.3.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html), [3.3.2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html)).
- Hint and error ids go in the control's [`aria-describedby`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby).
- On a wrong value, set [`aria-invalid="true"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid) and show the error as text ([WCAG 3.3.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html)).
- Native validation gets the same look through [`:user-invalid`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid), only after the user interacts.

### Specifications

- [WCAG 3.3.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html)
- [WCAG 3.3.2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html)
- [WCAG 1.3.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html)
- [MDN `aria-describedby`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby)
- [MDN `aria-invalid`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid)
- [MDN `:user-invalid`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid)
- [WCAG Use of color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)

### See also

- [Atoms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/components/atoms/field.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/field.css), [`examples/atoms/field.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/field.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Badge

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/badge.html

Inline status labels with tone variants that meet WCAG AA contrast.

### Live example

#### Tones

```html
<p class="cluster">
  <span data-badge>Draft</span>
  <span data-badge="accent">New</span>
  <span data-badge="success">Paid</span>
  <span data-badge="warning">Due soon</span>
  <span data-badge="danger">Overdue</span>
</p>
```

#### In context

```html
<section data-scroll="inline" aria-labelledby="invoices-caption" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="invoices-caption">Invoices</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr><th scope="col">Invoice</th><th scope="col">Status</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td>INV-031</td><td><span data-badge="success">Paid</span></td></tr>
      <tr><td>INV-032</td><td><span data-badge="danger">Overdue</span></td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</section>
```

### Attributes

`data-badge="neutral | accent | success | warning | danger"`

```text
data-badge="neutral | accent | success | warning | danger"
(empty means neutral)
```

- Static text. To make a badge clickable, put a real `<button>` or `<a href>` around it.
- An empty value is neutral.

### Accessibility

- The words carry the meaning, not the tone ([WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)); add "Status:" with `.visually-hidden` if only position gives context.
- Text on each tone has 4.5:1 contrast ([WCAG 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)), checked by `npm test`.

### Specifications

- [WCAG 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)
- [WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)
- [Using ARIA rule 1](https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1)

### See also

- [Atoms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/components/atoms/badge.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/badge.css), [`examples/atoms/badge.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/badge.html)

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent

## Molecules

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.html

Small groups of atoms that work as one unit. A level of [Atomic Design](https://atomicdesign.bradfrost.com/); APIs follow the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api).

### Our choices

From [`css/components/molecules/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/README.md).

- **Our choice:** native first, even where it differs from the APG example. The accordion is `<details name>`, so there are no heading wrappers and no arrow keys between headers (both optional in the APG); nav groups are `<details>` rather than scripted disclosure buttons, so they do not close on <kbd>Esc</kbd>. Both work with no script and keep find-in-page.
- **Our choice:** the drawer is a `<dialog>` variant (`data-dialog="drawer"`), not a new element or a popover, so it gets modality, inertness, focus handling and <kbd>Esc</kbd> from the browser. See [drawer.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/drawer.md).
- **Our choice:** dialog and drawer motion uses `@starting-style` and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`, declared after a plain transition, so engines without them simply open and close instantly. Duration tokens are `0s` under reduced motion.
- **Our choice:** anchored popovers fall back to the bottom center of the viewport where CSS anchor positioning is missing, rather than the browser's default center, so they never cover the middle of the content.
- **Our choice:** automatic tab activation (selection follows focus), as the [APG recommends](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/#deciding-when-to-make-selection-automatically-follow-focus) when panels show without delay; `activation="manual"` is one attribute away.
- **Our choice:** tabs are written as a `<nav>` of in-page links and `<section>` panels, so they read as a table of contents with JavaScript off. Once upgraded, each panel's first heading is visually hidden (it repeats the tab label) but stays in the accessibility tree.
- **Our choice:** `<dui-menu>` adds `role="menu"` and `role="menuitem"` itself. Without the script there are no menu roles, so assistive technology is never promised arrow keys that do not work. A list of links is never a menu; use a disclosure.
- **Our choice:** `<dui-toolbar>` keeps `role="toolbar"` in the markup, because a labelled group of Tab stops is still correct without the script; only the roving focus is added.
- **Our choice:** navigation lists (nav, tabs, pagination) drop the link underline, because their role is clear from the list ([F73](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F73) is about links in running text); hover brings it back. Breadcrumb links keep it, because they read as text.
- **Our choice:** "current" is never color alone: the nav item gets an accent bar, a tint and bold text; the current page in pagination is filled and bold; the selected tab gets a bar and full-strength text.
- **Our choice:** the current page in pagination stays a link with `aria-current="page"`, and a disabled Previous or Next is an `<a>` with no `href`, which HTML defines as a placeholder: not focusable and not a link. See [pagination.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/pagination.md).
- **Our choice:** a clickable card puts the link on its heading and stretches the link's hit area with a pseudo-element, so the card's accessible name is the heading and secondary actions in the footer stay separate links. See [card.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/card.md).
- **Our choice:** alert tones start with a word in the markup ("Warning:"), like the field's "Error:", and add a decorative icon drawn in CSS with empty alternative text.
- **Our choice:** an `info` tone with its own token (`--dui-color-info`) instead of reusing the accent, so a green or red brand accent never makes an informational message look like success or danger.
- **Our choice:** toasts never dismiss themselves and never take focus; each has a Dismiss button, and the region is a fixed element in the page (not a popover) so server-rendered messages show with JavaScript off. See [toast.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/toast.md).
- **Our choice:** the tooltip uses inverse colors (`--dui-color-surface-inverse` and `--dui-color-text-inverse`, derived from the text and surface tokens), so every theme gets a readable tooltip with no extra overrides.

### Not shipped, and why

| Candidate | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Combobox, typeahead, datalist | Later milestone (`dui-combobox`). It needs the APG Combobox pattern and a listbox, which is a bigger piece of work. |
| Vertical tabs | Not added. The APG allows them (`aria-orientation="vertical"`), but they need a different layout and Up/Down keys; add them with a real use case. |
| Menubar, submenus | Not added. Application menubars are rare on the web, and submenus are hard to use; a menu button covers actions. |
| Arrow-key navigation between accordion headers | Not added. It is optional in the APG Accordion pattern, and native `<details>` gives every summary a Tab stop. |
| Auto-dismissing toasts | Not added on purpose; see Our choices and [toast.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/toast.md). |
| `interestfor` tooltips | Not used yet. It is the coming standard for hover and focus invokers but ships only in Chromium; `<dui-tooltip>` does the job until it is interoperable. |

## Alerts

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.html

Status messages, from notices in the page to live alerts and toasts.

### Live example

#### Inline alerts

```html
<div class="stack">
  <div data-alert="info">
    <p><strong>Info:</strong> Maintenance is planned for Sunday at 02:00.</p>
  </div>
  <div data-alert="success">
    <p><strong>Success:</strong> Your changes were published.</p>
  </div>
  <div data-alert="warning">
    <p><strong>Warning:</strong> Your trial ends in 3 days.</p>
    <p><a href="#inline-title">Choose a plan</a> to keep your projects.</p>
  </div>
  <div data-alert="danger">
    <p><strong>Error:</strong> The file could not be uploaded. Try a file under 10 MB.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Live regions

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-announce="live-status">Save settings</button>
  <button type="button" data-announce="live-alert">Send without a subject</button>
</div>
<div id="live-status" role="status"></div>
<div id="live-alert" role="alert"></div>
```

#### Toasts

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-toast="success">Copy link</button>
  <button type="button" data-toast="info">Start export</button>
  <button type="button" data-toast="danger">Sync now</button>
</div>
```

### Attributes

```text
data-alert="info | success | warning | danger"   an inline alert with a tone
data-alert="toasts"                               the toast region (fixed position)
data-alert="dismiss"                              a toast's dismiss button
role="status" | role="alert"                      native ARIA live regions
```

### Accessibility

- New messages are announced without moving focus ([WCAG 4.1.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)): `role="status"` is polite, `role="alert"` interrupts. Static alerts need no role.
- Render the empty live region with the page and insert the text later ([ARIA22](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA22), [ARIA19](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA19)).
- Start the message with a word such as "Warning:", so tone is not color alone ([WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)).
- **Our choice:** toasts never dismiss themselves or take focus, so nobody loses a message ([WCAG 2.2.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable.html)).

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | reaches each toast's Dismiss button; toasts never take focus |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | on Dismiss, removes the toast and focuses the next one |

### Specifications

- [APG Alert pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/)
- [WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)
- [MDN `status` role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/status_role)
- [MDN `alert_role`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/alert_role)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/alerts.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/alerts.css), [`examples/molecules/alerts.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/alerts.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback)
- [Material Design 3: Snackbar](https://m3.material.io/components/snackbar/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Note](https://vercel.com/geist/note)

## Breadcrumb

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/breadcrumb.html

The path to the current page: an ordered list of links in a labelled `<nav>`.

### Live example

#### Breadcrumb

```html
<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb" data-breadcrumb>
  <ol>
    <li><a href="#trail-title">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="#trail-title">Molecules</a></li>
    <li><a href="#trail-title" aria-current="page">Breadcrumb</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

#### A long trail wraps

```html
<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb for the archive" data-breadcrumb>
  <ol>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Documentation</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Components and patterns</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Navigation</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Archive</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title" aria-current="page">Breadcrumbs in older releases</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

### Attributes

```text
data-breadcrumb       on <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
aria-current="page"   on the last link (native ARIA)
```

### Accessibility

- [`aria-current="page"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current) marks the current page, which is also bold ([WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)).
- Separators use CSS [alternative text](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/content#alternative_text) `""`, so they are not read.
- Links are at least 24px tall ([WCAG 2.5.8](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)).

### Keyboard

See the keyboard section of the [APG Breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/).

### Specifications

- [APG Breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/)
- [HTML `<nav>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element)
- [MDN `aria-current`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/breadcrumb.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/breadcrumb.css), [`examples/molecules/breadcrumb.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/breadcrumb.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Path controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/path-controls)
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Breadcrumbs](https://vercel.com/geist/breadcrumbs)

## Card

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.html

A self-contained item, such as an article teaser, on a raised surface.

**Our choice:** No standard exists: an `<article>` whose heading holds the one link, so the link name stays short.

### Live example

#### Cards in a grid

```html
<div class="grid" style="--grid-min: 16rem">
  <article data-card>
    <h3>Starter plan</h3>
    <p>For one person trying things out.</p>
    <p data-text="small muted">Free forever.</p>
    <footer>
      <a href="#grid-title" data-button="primary small">Choose Starter</a>
    </footer>
  </article>
  <article data-card="link">
    <img src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 160'%3E%3Crect width='320' height='160' fill='%233451d1'/%3E%3Ccircle cx='250' cy='40' r='60' fill='%238ea2ff'/%3E%3Crect x='24' y='96' width='140' height='40' rx='8' fill='%23f6f7f9'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="" width="320" height="160">
    <h3><a href="#grid-title">Theming guide</a></h3>
    <p>Override semantic tokens to make a theme, with no build step.</p>
    <footer>
      <span data-badge="accent">Guide</span>
      <a href="#grid-title" data-button="secondary small">View tokens</a>
    </footer>
  </article>
  <article data-card="link">
    <img src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 160'%3E%3Crect width='320' height='160' fill='%2317773a'/%3E%3Cpath d='M0 160 L120 50 L200 120 L260 70 L320 120 V160Z' fill='%235fd38d'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="" width="320" height="160">
    <h3><a href="#grid-title">Atoms</a></h3>
    <p>Buttons, switches, fields and badges.</p>
  </article>
</div>
```

### Attributes

```text
data-card          on <article> (or <section>, <li>): the card
data-card="link"   the whole card follows the link in its heading
Children: an optional first <img> (or <picture>, <video>) as media,
a heading, body content, and an optional <footer> for actions.
```

### Accessibility

- Every card has a heading. Use `<article>` when it stands on its own.
- Images need `alt`, or `alt=""` when decorative.
- `data-card="link"` stretches the heading's link over the card, so the link name is the heading ([Inclusive Components](https://inclusive-components.design/cards/)). Footer actions stay focusable; card text cannot be selected with the mouse.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to each card's heading link, then to its footer actions |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | follows the focused link |

### Specifications

- [HTML `<article>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-article-element)
- [WCAG Link purpose in context](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context.html)
- [WCAG Focus visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html)
- [W3C images](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/card.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/card.css), [`examples/molecules/card.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/card.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- [Material Design 3: Cards](https://m3.material.io/components/cards/overview)
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Dialog and drawer

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.html

A modal `<dialog>`, either centered or as a drawer along one edge of the viewport.

### Live example

#### Modal dialog

```html
<button type="button" commandfor="confirm-dialog" command="show-modal">Delete project…</button>
<dialog id="confirm-dialog" data-dialog aria-labelledby="confirm-dialog-title">
  <header>
    <h2 id="confirm-dialog-title">Delete project?</h2>
  </header>
  <p>This deletes the project and its 12 files for everyone. You cannot undo it.</p>
  <form method="dialog">
    <footer>
      <button type="submit" value="cancel" data-button="secondary" autofocus>Cancel</button>
      <button type="submit" value="delete">Delete project</button>
    </footer>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

#### Drawer (end)

```html
<button type="button" commandfor="filters-drawer" command="show-modal">Filters</button>
<dialog id="filters-drawer" data-dialog="drawer end" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="filters-drawer-title">
  <header>
    <h2 id="filters-drawer-title">Filters</h2>
    <button type="button" commandfor="filters-drawer" command="close" data-button="quiet small">Close</button>
  </header>
  <form method="dialog" class="stack">
    <fieldset>
      <legend>Status</legend>
      <label><input type="checkbox" name="show-open" checked> Open</label>
      <label><input type="checkbox" name="show-closed"> Closed</label>
    </fieldset>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="filters-owner">Owner</label>
      <input id="filters-owner" name="owner" type="text" autocomplete="off">
    </div>
    <footer>
      <button type="submit" value="apply">Apply filters</button>
    </footer>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

#### Drawer (start)

```html
<button type="button" commandfor="menu-drawer" command="show-modal">Menu</button>
<dialog id="menu-drawer" data-dialog="drawer start" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="menu-drawer-title">
  <header>
    <h2 id="menu-drawer-title">Menu</h2>
    <button type="button" commandfor="menu-drawer" command="close" data-button="quiet small">Close</button>
  </header>
  <nav aria-label="Drawer" data-nav>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#menu-drawer-title" aria-current="page">Overview</a></li>
      <li><a href="#drawer-start-title">Projects</a></li>
      <li><a href="#drawer-start-title">Settings</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
</dialog>
```

#### Non-modal dialog

```html
<button type="button" data-show-dialog="note-dialog">Show a note</button>
<dialog id="note-dialog" data-dialog closedby="closerequest" aria-labelledby="note-dialog-title">
  <header>
    <h2 id="note-dialog-title">Autosave is on</h2>
    <button type="button" commandfor="note-dialog" command="close" data-button="quiet small">Close</button>
  </header>
  <p>Changes are saved as you type.</p>
</dialog>
```

### Attributes

```text
data-dialog                         on <dialog>: header, body and footer layout
                                    and the open transition
data-dialog="drawer [start | end]"  a drawer at the inline-start or inline-end
                                    edge (end is the default)
closedby="any | closerequest | none"  native: how the dialog can be dismissed
Children: an optional <header> (heading and close button) and <footer>
(actions, end-aligned); everything else is the body.
```

### Accessibility

- `showModal()` or `command="show-modal"` makes the page inert, moves focus in and returns it on close.
- Name each dialog with `aria-labelledby`. Put `autofocus` on the least destructive action.
- <kbd>Esc</kbd> and the close buttons always work ([WCAG 2.1.2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap.html)); [`closedby="any"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog#closedby) adds light dismiss.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | on an opener, opens the dialog and moves focus into it |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to the next focusable element inside the dialog / Shift+Tab: previous |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | closes the dialog and returns focus to the opener |

### Specifications

- [HTML `<dialog>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element)
- [APG Dialog (Modal) pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)
- [MDN `<dialog>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog)
- [MDN `Invoker_Commands_API`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API)
- [MDN `@starting-style`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@starting-style)
- [MDN `transition-behavior`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/transition-behavior)
- [WCAG Animation from interactions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html)

### See also

- [Organisms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/organisms/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/dialog.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/dialog.css), [`examples/molecules/dialog.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/dialog.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Modality](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/modality)
- [Material Design 3: Dialogs](https://m3.material.io/components/dialogs/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Modal](https://vercel.com/geist/modal)

## Disclosure

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/disclosure.html

A summary that shows or hides more content, built on `<details>` and `<summary>`.

### Live example

#### Disclosure

```html
<details>
  <summary>What is included in the plan?</summary>
  <p>Unlimited projects, five collaborators and email support.</p>
</details>
```

#### Exclusive accordion

```html
<div data-disclosure="accordion">
  <details name="faq" open>
    <summary>Shipping</summary>
    <p>Orders ship within two working days.</p>
  </details>
  <details name="faq">
    <summary>Returns</summary>
    <p>Return unused items within 30 days for a full refund.</p>
  </details>
  <details name="faq">
    <summary>Warranty</summary>
    <p>Every product has a two-year warranty.</p>
  </details>
</div>
```

#### Accordion with several open

```html
<div data-disclosure="accordion">
  <details>
    <summary>Monthly plan</summary>
    <p>Pay each month and cancel any time.</p>
  </details>
  <details>
    <summary>Yearly plan</summary>
    <p>Pay once a year and get two months free.</p>
  </details>
</div>
```

#### Inline show more

```html
<p>The release adds pagination, tabs and toasts.</p>
<details data-disclosure="plain">
  <summary>Show the full list of changes</summary>
  <ul>
    <li>Twelve molecules with example pages.</li>
    <li>Five small web components.</li>
    <li>Four explainers for custom patterns.</li>
  </ul>
</details>
```

### Attributes

```text
data-disclosure="accordion"   on a wrapper around several <details>:
                              joins them into one bordered block
data-disclosure="plain"       on a <details>: no box, for "Show more"
                              text inside prose
name="group"                  on each <details> (native): only one open
open                          on a <details> (native): open on load
```

### Accessibility

- `<summary>` is a button with `aria-expanded` ([HTML-AAM](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-summary)); no ARIA to write.
- Unlike the [APG Accordion](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/), headers are not headings and have no arrow keys; both are optional there.
- Avoid exclusive groups ([`name`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details#name)) when people compare sections.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to the next summary / Shift+Tab: previous |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | opens or closes the focused section |

### Specifications

- [HTML `<details>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element)
- [APG Disclosure pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/)
- [MDN `details`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/disclosure.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/disclosure.css), [`examples/molecules/disclosure.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/disclosure.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Disclosure controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/disclosure-controls)
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Collapse](https://vercel.com/geist/collapse)

## Menu button

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.html

A button that opens a menu of actions.

### Live example

#### Actions menu

```html
<dui-menu>
  <button type="button" popovertarget="row-actions">Actions</button>
  <div id="row-actions" popover data-popover>
    <button type="button">Edit</button>
    <button type="button">Duplicate</button>
    <button type="button">Archive</button>
    <hr>
    <button type="button">Delete</button>
  </div>
</dui-menu>
<p role="status" id="menu-result"></p>
```

#### Links are not a menu

```html
<button type="button" popovertarget="account-links">Account</button>
<div id="account-links" popover data-popover>
  <nav aria-label="Account" data-nav>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#links-title">Profile</a></li>
      <li><a href="#links-title">Billing</a></li>
      <li><a href="#links-title">Sign out</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
</div>
```

### Attributes

```text
<dui-menu>                         wraps the button and its popover
popovertarget="menu-id"            on the <button> (native)
popover data-popover               on the menu element
<button> or <a href> children      the actions; <hr> separates groups
Added by the component: aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, role="menu",
role="menuitem", tabindex="-1".
```

### Accessibility

- `<dui-menu>` adds the ARIA and arrow keys. Without JavaScript, every action is a Tab stop.
- For links to other pages, use a disclosure: `role="menu"` means arrow keys and no Tab stops ([APG note](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/)).

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> / <kbd>Down Arrow</kbd> | on the button, opens the menu and focuses the first item |
| <kbd>Up Arrow</kbd> | on the button, opens the menu and focuses the last item |
| <kbd>Down Arrow</kbd> / <kbd>Up Arrow</kbd> | next or previous item, wrapping |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | first or last item |
| <kbd>A letter</kbd> | next item whose label starts with it |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | activates the item and closes the menu |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | closes the menu and returns focus to the button |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | closes the menu and moves on |

### Specifications

- [APG Menu Button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/)
- [APG Menu and Menubar pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/)
- [MDN `menu_role`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/menu_role)
- [MDN `aria-haspopup`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-haspopup)
- [WHATWG popover](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/menu-button.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/menu-button.css), [`examples/molecules/menu-button.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/menu-button.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Pull-down buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pull-down-buttons)
- [Material Design 3: Menus](https://m3.material.io/components/menus/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Menu](https://vercel.com/geist/menu)

## Pagination

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.html

Links to the pages of a long list of results.

**Our choice:** No standard exists: a labelled `<nav>` with a list of links and `aria-current="page"`, as for breadcrumbs.

### Live example

#### Middle of a long list

```html
<nav aria-label="Pagination" data-pagination>
  <ul>
    <li><a href="?page=4" rel="prev">Previous<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=1"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>1</a></li>
    <li aria-hidden="true">…</li>
    <li><a href="?page=4"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>4</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=5" aria-current="page"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>5</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=6"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>6</a></li>
    <li aria-hidden="true">…</li>
    <li><a href="?page=10"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>10</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=6" rel="next">Next<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

#### First page

```html
<nav aria-label="Pagination, search results" data-pagination>
  <ul>
    <li><a>Previous<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=1" aria-current="page"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>1</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=2"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>2</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=3"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>3</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=2" rel="next">Next<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

### Attributes

```text
data-pagination        on <nav aria-label="Pagination">
aria-current="page"    on the current page link (native ARIA)
<a> without href       a disabled Previous or Next (native placeholder link)
<li aria-hidden="true">…</li>   a gap in the page numbers
```

### Accessibility

- A visually hidden "Page" completes each number's link name ([WCAG 2.4.4](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context.html)).
- At the ends, Previous or Next is an `<a>` with no `href`: not focusable.
- **Our choice:** the current page stays a link with `aria-current="page"`, so the list count stays stable.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to the next page link / Shift+Tab: previous |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | follows the focused link |

### Specifications

- [HTML `<nav>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element)
- [MDN `aria-current`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current)
- [WHATWG link type next](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-next)
- [WHATWG the a element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element)
- [WCAG Target size minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/pagination.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/pagination.css), [`examples/molecules/pagination.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/pagination.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Pagination](https://vercel.com/geist/pagination)

## Popover

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/popover.html

Content shown on top of the page from a button, with the `popover` attribute.

### Live example

#### Popover

```html
<button type="button" popovertarget="share-popover">Share</button>
<div id="share-popover" popover data-popover>
  <p>Anyone with the link can view this page.</p>
</div>
```

#### Above the button, with a close button

```html
<button type="button" popovertarget="help-popover">Help</button>
<div id="help-popover" popover="manual" data-popover="block-start">
  <p><strong>Need a hand?</strong></p>
  <p>Read the <a href="#above-title">guide</a> or ask in the forum.</p>
  <button type="button" popovertarget="help-popover" popovertargetaction="hide" data-button="small">Close</button>
</div>
```

#### Tooltip

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <dui-tooltip>
    <button type="button" aria-describedby="save-tip">Save</button>
    <span id="save-tip" popover="hint" role="tooltip">Shortcut: Ctrl+S</span>
  </dui-tooltip>
  <dui-tooltip>
    <button type="button" aria-label="Copy link" aria-describedby="copy-tip" data-button="quiet">⧉</button>
    <span id="copy-tip" popover="hint" role="tooltip">Copies the page address</span>
  </dui-tooltip>
</div>
```

### Attributes

```text
data-popover                    on a [popover] element: panel look, anchored
                                below the invoker, aligned to its start edge
data-popover="block-start | inline-start | inline-end"
                                place it above or beside the invoker instead
role="tooltip"                  on a [popover] element: tooltip look,
                                placed above the trigger
popover="auto | manual | hint"  native: auto light-dismisses, manual does not
```

### Accessibility

- A popover does not trap focus; decisions belong in a modal `<dialog>`. For actions, use the [menu button](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.md).
- A tooltip supplements the trigger's name, shows on focus and hover, and closes on <kbd>Esc</kbd> ([WCAG 1.4.13](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html); [APG Tooltip](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/) is a draft).

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | on a popover button, opens or closes the popover |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves into the open popover, then on through the page |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | closes an auto popover and returns focus to its button |
| <kbd>Tab to a tooltip trigger</kbd> | shows its tooltip / Esc: hides it, focus stays |

### Specifications

- [HTML `popover` attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#the-popover-attribute)
- [MDN Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API)
- [WHATWG popover](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html)
- [MDN `popover`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/popover)
- [MDN `CSS_anchor_positioning`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_anchor_positioning)
- [MDN `position-area`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/position-area)
- [MDN `position-try-fallbacks`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/position-try-fallbacks)
- [W3C css anchor position 1](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/)
- [Open UI interest invokers.explainer](https://open-ui.org/components/interest-invokers.explainer/)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/popover.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/popover.css), [`examples/molecules/popover.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/popover.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Popovers](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers)
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Search

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/search.html

A search form in a `<search>` landmark with an `<input type="search">`.

### Live example

#### With a visible label

```html
<search aria-label="Guides">
  <form action="search.html" method="get">
    <label for="guide-search">Search the guides</label>
    <input id="guide-search" type="search" name="q" autocomplete="off" aria-describedby="guide-search-hint">
    <button type="submit">Search</button>
    <p id="guide-search-hint" data-field="hint">Try "tokens" or "dialog".</p>
  </form>
</search>
```

#### Compact, label visually hidden

```html
<search aria-label="Site">
  <form action="search.html" method="get">
    <label for="site-search" class="visually-hidden">Search this site</label>
    <input id="site-search" type="search" name="q" autocomplete="off">
    <button type="submit" data-button="secondary">Search</button>
  </form>
</search>
```

### Attributes

```text
<search> > <form> with an <input type="search">   no attribute needed:
the label and any hint span the full width, the input and the submit
button share the row below.
```

### Accessibility

- `<search>` is a landmark; label it only when there are several.
- The input needs a `<label>`, visually hidden if space is short; a placeholder is not a label ([WCAG 3.3.2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html)).

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | in the field, submits the search |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | in the field, clears it (in browsers that support it) |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves from the field to the button |

### Specifications

- [HTML `<search>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-search-element)
- [MDN `<input type="search">`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/search)
- [MDN `<search>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/search)
- [W3C labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/search.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/search.css), [`examples/molecules/search.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/search.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Search fields](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/search-fields)
- [Material Design 3: Search](https://m3.material.io/components/search/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Search Input](https://vercel.com/geist/search-input)

## Site navigation

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/nav.html

The main links of a site in a `<nav>` landmark, with the current page marked.

### Live example

#### Vertical (sidebar)

```html
<nav aria-label="Sidebar example" data-nav="vertical">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#vertical-title">Overview</a></li>
    <li>
      <details open>
        <summary>Projects</summary>
        <ul>
          <li><a href="#vertical-title" aria-current="page">Active</a></li>
          <li><a href="#vertical-title">Archived</a></li>
        </ul>
      </details>
    </li>
    <li>
      <details>
        <summary>Settings</summary>
        <ul>
          <li><a href="#vertical-title">Profile</a></li>
          <li><a href="#vertical-title">Billing</a></li>
        </ul>
      </details>
    </li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

#### Horizontal (top bar)

```html
<nav aria-label="Top bar example" data-nav="horizontal">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#horizontal-title" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
    <li>
      <details name="top-bar">
        <summary>Products</summary>
        <ul>
          <li><a href="#horizontal-title">Design system</a></li>
          <li><a href="#horizontal-title">Icons</a></li>
        </ul>
      </details>
    </li>
    <li>
      <details name="top-bar">
        <summary>Company</summary>
        <ul>
          <li><a href="#horizontal-title">About</a></li>
          <li><a href="#horizontal-title">Careers</a></li>
        </ul>
      </details>
    </li>
    <li><a href="#horizontal-title">Contact</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

### Attributes

```text
data-nav="vertical | horizontal"   on <nav> (empty means vertical)
aria-current="page"                on the current link (native ARIA)
<details> / <summary>              inside an <li> for a collapsible group;
                                   open to expand it on load, name for
                                   one-at-a-time
```

### Accessibility

- Native `<details>` in place of the [APG disclosure navigation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/); not an ARIA menu.
- [`aria-current="page"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current) is shown with a bar, a tint and bold text ([WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)).
- Give each `<nav>` a distinct `aria-label` when there are several.
- Groups do not close on <kbd>Esc</kbd>; <kbd>Enter</kbd> on the summary does.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to the next link or group summary / Shift+Tab: previous |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | on a summary, opens or closes the group |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | on a link, follows it |

### Specifications

- [HTML `<nav>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element)
- [APG Landmark regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/)
- [APG Disclosure navigation example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/)
- [MDN `aria-current`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current)
- [MDN `nav`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/nav)
- [WCAG F73](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F73)
- [WHATWG the details element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element)
- [WCAG Non text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)

### See also

- [Organisms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/organisms/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/nav.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/nav.css), [`examples/molecules/nav.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/nav.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Tabs

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.html

Sections of content shown one at a time, chosen from a list of tabs.

### Live example

#### Automatic activation

```html
<dui-tabs>
  <nav aria-label="Account settings">
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#tab-profile">Profile</a></li>
      <li><a href="#tab-security">Security</a></li>
      <li><a href="#tab-notifications">Notifications</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
  <section id="tab-profile">
    <h3>Profile</h3>
    <p>Your name and photo appear on comments and shared projects.</p>
  </section>
  <section id="tab-security">
    <h3>Security</h3>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="tab-security-code">Recovery code</label>
      <input id="tab-security-code" name="recovery" type="text" autocomplete="off">
    </div>
  </section>
  <section id="tab-notifications">
    <h3>Notifications</h3>
    <p>Email alerts are on. You get a weekly digest on Mondays.</p>
  </section>
</dui-tabs>
```

#### Manual activation

```html
<dui-tabs activation="manual">
  <nav aria-label="Report period">
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#tab-week">Week</a></li>
      <li><a href="#tab-month" aria-current="true">Month</a></li>
      <li><a href="#tab-year">Year</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
  <section id="tab-week">
    <h3>Week</h3>
    <p>42 orders this week.</p>
  </section>
  <section id="tab-month">
    <h3>Month</h3>
    <p>180 orders this month.</p>
  </section>
  <section id="tab-year">
    <h3>Year</h3>
    <p>2,140 orders this year.</p>
  </section>
</dui-tabs>
```

#### Right to left

```html
<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <dui-tabs>
    <nav aria-label="الإعدادات">
      <ul>
        <li><a href="#tab-rtl-general">عام</a></li>
        <li><a href="#tab-rtl-privacy">الخصوصية</a></li>
        <li><a href="#tab-rtl-help">مساعدة</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
    <section id="tab-rtl-general">
      <h3>عام</h3>
      <p>الإعدادات العامة للحساب.</p>
    </section>
    <section id="tab-rtl-privacy">
      <h3>الخصوصية</h3>
      <p>من يمكنه رؤية ملفك الشخصي.</p>
    </section>
    <section id="tab-rtl-help">
      <h3>مساعدة</h3>
      <p>الأسئلة الشائعة والدعم.</p>
    </section>
  </dui-tabs>
</div>
```

### Attributes

```text
<dui-tabs>                 wraps a <nav aria-label> with a list of
                           <a href="#panel-id"> links, then the panels
activation="manual"        on <dui-tabs>: arrows move focus, Enter or
                           Space selects (default: automatic)
aria-current="true"        on a link: the tab selected on load (else the
                           tab named in the URL fragment, else the first).
                           The component swaps it for aria-selected;
                           aria-selected is not allowed on a link.
role="tablist" | "tab" | "tabpanel" (added by the component; styled here)
```

### Accessibility

- The selected tab has a bar and full-strength text, not color alone ([WCAG 1.4.11](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)).
- Without JavaScript, every section shows and the links work as a table of contents.
- **Our choice:** automatic activation, as the [APG recommends](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/#deciding-when-to-make-selection-automatically-follow-focus) for fast panels; `activation="manual"` otherwise.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves into the tab list (to the selected tab), then to the panel |
| <kbd>Right Arrow</kbd> / <kbd>Left Arrow</kbd> | next or previous tab, wrapping (swapped in right-to-left) |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | first or last tab |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | selects the focused tab (manual activation) |

### Specifications

- [APG Tabs pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/)
- [MDN `tab_role`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/tab_role)
- [MDN `tabpanel_role`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/tabpanel_role)
- [W3C el nav](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-nav)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/tabs.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/tabs.css), [`examples/molecules/tabs.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/tabs.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Tab views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/tab-views)
- [Material Design 3: Tabs](https://m3.material.io/components/tabs/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Tabs](https://vercel.com/geist/tabs)

## Toolbar

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/toolbar.html

A row of related controls that is one stop in the tab order.

### Live example

#### Text formatting

```html
<dui-toolbar role="toolbar" aria-label="Text formatting">
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="true">Bold</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">Italic</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">Underline</button>
  <hr>
  <button type="button">Insert link</button>
  <button type="button">Clear formatting</button>
</dui-toolbar>
```

#### Vertical

```html
<dui-toolbar role="toolbar" aria-label="Drawing tools" aria-orientation="vertical">
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="true">Select</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">Pen</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">Eraser</button>
</dui-toolbar>
```

### Attributes

```text
role="toolbar" aria-label="…"     on the container (<dui-toolbar> or any element)
aria-orientation="vertical"       optional; default horizontal
aria-pressed="true | false"       on toggle buttons (native ARIA)
<hr>                              a separator between groups of controls
```

### Accessibility

- Use a toolbar for three or more controls. Without JavaScript, each control is a Tab stop.
- Toggle buttons use [`aria-pressed`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-pressed), shown by more than color ([WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)).

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves into the toolbar (to the last focused control), then out of it |
| <kbd>Right Arrow</kbd> / <kbd>Left Arrow</kbd> | next or previous control, wrapping (swapped in right-to-left) |
| <kbd>Down Arrow</kbd> / <kbd>Up Arrow</kbd> | the same in a vertical toolbar |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | first or last control |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | activates the focused button |

### Specifications

- [APG Toolbar pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/)
- [MDN `toolbar_role`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/toolbar_role)
- [APG kbd roving tabindex](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_roving_tabindex)

### See also

- [Molecules](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.md)
- Source: [`css/components/molecules/toolbar.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/toolbar.css), [`examples/molecules/toolbar.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/toolbar.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Toolbars](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toolbars)
- [Material Design 3: Toolbars](https://m3.material.io/components/toolbars/overview)
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## App shell

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.html

The frame of an application: header, primary sidebar, main content and an optional auxiliary sidebar.

**Our choice:** No standard defines an app shell: the landmarks `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<aside>`, placed with CSS grid.

Coming in M3b.

### Specifications

- [APG Landmark regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/)
- [HTML `<main>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-main-element)
- [HTML `<aside>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-aside-element)
- [WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

### See also

- [Layouts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/index.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Sidebars](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sidebars)
- [Material Design 3: Scaffold](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/scaffold/overview)
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Split

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/split.html

Two regions side by side at a set ratio, stacked on narrow screens.

**Our choice:** No standard exists for a fixed split: two regions in a CSS grid. A draggable divider would follow the APG Window Splitter pattern.

Coming in M3b.

### Specifications

- [APG Window Splitter pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/)
- [WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

### See also

- [Layouts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/index.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Split views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/split-views)
- [Material Design 3: Scaffold: Panes](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/scaffold/panes)
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent
